clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. The President’ s Board shall 
conduct an objective review of the for­
eign intelligence activities of the Govern­
ment and of the performance of the 
functions of the Central Intelligence 
Agency and shall report its findings to 
the President semi-annually or at more 
frequent intervals as the President’ s 
Board may deem appropriate. Such re­
ports shall embrace the quality of the 
foreign intelligence provided to the Ex­
ecutive Branch of the Government, the 
Performance by the Central Intelligence 
Agency of its functions, the performance 
of their respective foreign intelligence 
functions by the principal intelligence 
elements of executive departments and 
other agencies, and any other related 
foreign intelligence matter which the 
President’ s Board deems appropriate.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. The members of the President’ s 
Board, individually and sitting as the 
President’ s Board, shall consult from 
time to time with the Director of Central 
Intelligence concerning the activities of 
the Central Intelligence Agency and with 
intelligence elements of other depart­
ments and agencies. The Director of 
Central Intelligence and the intelligence 
elements concerned are authorized to 
make available to the President’ s Board 
or to its individual members any infor­
mation concerning foreign intelligence 
activities relating to the national interest 
which the President’ s Board or its mem­
bers may require to fulfill their responsi­
bilities to the President under this order.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text:
Sec. 4. Each member of the President’ s 
Board shall execute an undertaking not 
to reveal any classified information ob­
tained by virtue of his service on the 
President’ s Board except to the President 
or to such persons as the President may 
designate.

clauses.label: Sec. 5.
clauses.text:
Sec. 5. The transportation and per- 
diem allowances referred to in section 1  
of this order, and any other expenditures 
arising in connection with the activities 
of the President’ s Board, shall be paid 
from the appropriation appearing under 
the heading “Special Projects” in Title I 
of the General Government Matters Ap­
propriation Act, 1956 (Public Law 110, 
approved June 29, 1955), without regard 
to the provisions of section 3681 of the 
Revised Statutes and section 9 of the Act 
of March 4, 1909, 35 Stat. 1027, (31
U. S. C. 672 and 673).
S ec. 6. This order shall be effective as 
of January 13,1956.

Establishing  the P resident ’s B oard op

Activities
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
as President of the United States, and in 
order to enhance the security of the 
United States and the conduct of its for­
eign affairs by furthering the availability 
of intelligence of the highest order, it is 
ordered as follows:
Section L There is hereby established 
the President’ s Board of Consultants on 
Foreign Intelligence Activities, herein­
after referred to as the President’ s 
Board. The members of the President’ s 
Board shall be appointed by the Presi­
dent, from among persons outside the 
Government and on the basis of ability, 
experience, and knowledge of matters re­
lating to the national defense and se­
curity, and shall serve without compen­
sation, but may receive transportation 
and per-diem allowances as authorized 
by law for persons serving without 
compensation.
Sec. 2. The President’ s Board shall 
conduct an objective review of the for­
eign intelligence activities of the Govern­
ment and of the performance of the 
functions of the Central Intelligence 
Agency and shall report its findings to 
the President semi-annually or at more 
frequent intervals as the President’ s 
Board may deem appropriate. Such re­
ports shall embrace the quality of the 
foreign intelligence provided to the Ex­
ecutive Branch of the Government, the 
Performance by the Central Intelligence 
Agency of its functions, the performance 
of their respective foreign intelligence 
functions by the principal intelligence 
elements of executive departments and 
other agencies, and any other related 
foreign intelligence matter which the 
President’ s Board deems appropriate.
Sec. 3. The members of the President’ s 
Board, individually and sitting as the 
President’ s Board, shall consult from 
time to time with the Director of Central 
Intelligence concerning the activities of 
the Central Intelligence Agency and with 
intelligence elements of other depart­
ments and agencies. The Director of 
Central Intelligence and the intelligence 
elements concerned are authorized to 
make available to the President’ s Board 
or to its individual members any infor­
mation concerning foreign intelligence 
activities relating to the national interest 
which the President’ s Board or its mem­
bers may require to fulfill their responsi­
bilities to the President under this order.
Sec. 4. Each member of the President’ s 
Board shall execute an undertaking not 
to reveal any classified information ob­
tained by virtue of his service on the 
President’ s Board except to the President 
or to such persons as the President may 
designate.
Sec. 5. The transportation and per- 
diem allowances referred to in section 1  
of this order, and any other expenditures 
arising in connection with the activities 
of the President’ s Board, shall be paid 
from the appropriation appearing under 
the heading “Special Projects” in Title I 
of the General Government Matters Ap­
propriation Act, 1956 (Public Law 110, 
approved June 29, 1955), without regard 
to the provisions of section 3681 of the 
Revised Statutes and section 9 of the Act 
of March 4, 1909, 35 Stat. 1027, (31
U. S. C. 672 and 673).
S ec. 6. This order shall be effective as 
of January 13,1956.
D wight  D. E isenhower
T he W hite  H ouse ,
February 6,1956.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 10656 (21 FR 859, Feb. 8, 1956, signed Feb. 6, 1956): secs. 1-5 establish the President's Board of Consultants on Foreign Intelligence Activities (appointment of outside members, review of foreign intelligence activities with semi-annual reports to the President, consultation with the Director of Central Intelligence, security undertakings and payment of allowances from the 'Special Projects' appropriation); it has no own term and no savings clause. I read the held full text of EO 10938 (26 FR 3951, May 6, 1961, signed May 4, 1961, Establishing the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board): secs. 1-3 create the successor Board and sec. 4 states 'Executive Order No. 10656 of February 6, 1956, is hereby revoked.' That names EO 10656 by number and date and reaches all of it with no exception. The successor Board is a replacement, but the ending text is an express revocation, so this is not a successor-body inference. D6 self-check: a text search of the held full-run texts finds EO 10656 named only in EO 10938 (and its neighbouring-page extract in EO 10939, which carries the same page). EO 10938 was itself revoked by EO 11460 sec. 6 (held), which creates a new Board and does not mention EO 10656, so the revocation of the revoking order does not revive 10656. Nothing amends, extends or re-delegates EO 10656 between 1956 and 1961, and no own term ran out earlier. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 10938' agrees; the 1989 snapshot row is empty. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing May 4, 1961, no later date stated) is not otherwise adjudicated.
